proposition: Bākharzī reports that Jāmī dismissed Yazdī's career, and Ibn Turka's by extension, telling Yazdī he had given himself over to amirs and bureaucrats and made a weak defence of Sufism; Bākharzī adds Shirvānī's comparison finding Jāmī the sounder and Yazdī's work accused of heterodoxy. This is Jāmī's opinion as relayed by his own hagiographer; MK does not vouch for it.

mediation.who: Jāmī and Yazdī on the bank of the Injīl canal, Herat, after 850/1446
mediation.note: MK supposes Jāmī in his late thirties and Yazdī in his late seventies or early eighties; the encounter is known only from Bākharzī

mediation.who: ʿAbd al-Vāsiʿ Niẓāmī Bākharzī, Maqāmāt-i Jāmī
mediation.note: hostile hagiographer; MK: 'king-of-the-hill tendentiousness'; MK is translating a hostile reporter
Jāmī saw a first draft (Binbaş), so the words may be his, but MK only says 'may be supposed'
